dem_aspect — DEM surface op

• Data kinds: depth → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.dem_aspect(dem, cell_size, method='horn', flat_tol=1e-12) (to call the implementation directly, import demops; demops.dem_aspect(dem, cell_size, method='horn', flat_tol=1e-12); from the registry, opsdem.get("dem_aspect"))

Usage

Slope aspect [degrees]. North is 0 degrees, increasing towards east. Flat cells get ASPECT_FLAT.

Flat cells are not returned as 0 because 0 would mean "north-facing slope" —— returning an indistinguishable value is the textbook case of being wrong without raising.

Procedure: take the same 3x3 gradient (dz/dx, dz/dy) as dem_slope, convert the direction of the downhill gradient atan2(-dz/dx, -dz/dy) to degrees and wrap it into [0, 360). Assuming row 0 is north and the direction of increasing column is east: north 0 / east 90 / south 180 / west 270. Passing a grid whose row 0 is south (a vertically flipped array) swaps north and south, and no exception is raised.

• dem, cell_size, method: same contract as dem_slope (3x3 or larger, nan for missing data, sentinel values rejected, cell_size positive [m]).

• flat_tol: if the gradient magnitude hypot(dz/dx, dz/dy) [m/m] is at or below this, the cell is treated as flat and ASPECT_FLAT (= -1.0) is returned. The default 1e-12 covers only "numerically exactly flat". Even flat land with integer elevations can get an aspect from tiny gradients, so stating a meaningful threshold (e.g. 1e-3) explicitly is advisable.

• Return value: (H, W) float64. [0, 360) or -1.0. Around nan cells, nan.

• When taking a histogram or mean of aspects, remove -1 first (out >= 0).
